questions.description: How do activity or total expenditure estimates agree with reference measurements?
questions.gap: Specific device, construct, time window, repeated-change reliability and calibration required.

questions.description: How variable are comparable body-mass observations under defined conditions?
questions.gap: No universal tissue-change detection threshold or sampling window.

questions.description: How do weight-based models estimate changes in intake against reference intake-balance methods?
questions.gap: Absolute TEE, athlete transfer and decision benefit not established.

questions.description: How do different planned loss rates affect athlete body composition?
questions.gap: Different duration and realized exposure; no universal safe loss rate or hybrid policy.

questions.description: How should eligible reported intake and weight response inform nutrition review?
questions.gap: Structural ambiguity, reporting stability and prospective decision value require review.

claims.assertion: In the small controlled maintenance sample, group mean intake was close to DLW expenditure but individual ratios differed.
claims.limitations: Six adults, inpatient control and weight bound; no equivalence test or free-living log validation.
claims.assessment: Study-specific descriptive agreement, not a general error distribution.

support.result: Intake 2390 ±543 vs DLW 2373 ±713 kcal/day; mean ratio 1.03 ±0.15, range 0.87–1.27.
support.restriction: Constant controlled food intake during ten-day balance period.

claims.assertion: The pooled standardized difference between Ten-Haaf predicted and measured RMR was near zero in the assessed athlete comparisons.
claims.limitations: Four studies, seven comparisons, 204 participants; possible local derivation bias and heterogeneous methods; not equivalence.
claims.assessment: Accuracy of group estimate is not individual precision or TEE validity.

support.restriction: Resting energy expenditure only; no PAL or exercise estimate.

claims.assertion: The review reported that 80.2% of participants in its Ten-Haaf precision synthesis had predictions within 10% of measured RMR.
claims.limitations: Precision subset differs from accuracy subset; verify exact denominator and overlap; 10% is study criterion not personal uncertainty.
claims.assessment: Prediction agreement criterion, not reliability or confidence interval.

support.restriction: Not a claim of TEE accuracy; verify individual denominator before approval.

claims.assertion: None of seven studied wrist devices achieved median energy expenditure error below 20% in the reported laboratory comparison.
claims.limitations: Older specific devices, seated/walk/run/cycle tasks; no daily TEE or strength-specific validation.
claims.assessment: Check exact error definition and strata; not signed correction.

support.result: No device median EE error below 20%.
support.restriction: Laboratory tasks; does not quantify current devices or longitudinal change.

claims.assertion: The tested accelerometer-based TEE method overestimated mean DLW expenditure in this runner sample.
claims.limitations: 16 young women, single method and seven-day period; no repeated change validation or hybrid population.
claims.assessment: Criterion agreement, not causal effect; no universal correction.

support.locator: Results Fig. 2B-2; Methods DLW and triaxial accelerometer
support.result: Bias +416 ±242 kcal/day (~12.5%); LoA −59 to +891 kcal/day; r=.828.
support.restriction: Waist Actimarker EW4800 PAL/BMR method; not other devices.

claims.assertion: Ten of twelve tested wearable PAEE estimates were significantly below the DLW-derived PAEE comparator.
claims.limitations: 19 adults; comparator subtracts BMR and assumed TEF; devices outdated; no equivalence from nonsignificance.
claims.assessment: Device-count finding not person-level error or total expenditure.

support.result: Reference PAEE 728.0 ±162.7 kcal/day; 10/12 devices significantly underestimated.
support.restriction: Residual PAEE, not TEE; verify multiplicity and device-level results.

claims.assertion: First-morning body mass varied across days in active men exercising in heat under fluid replacement guidance.
claims.limitations: Retrospective; specific environment, sex and hydration protocol; no tissue inference.
claims.assessment: Descriptive variability not universal minimum detectable change.

claims.assertion: The model-estimated changes in intake were close to intake-balance estimates at group level but showed substantial individual disagreement.
claims.limitations: 140 CALERIE restriction participants; reference estimated, not independent absolute intake; body-weight model assumptions and selected completers; not daily EE.
claims.assessment: Change from baseline only; agreement not prospective hybrid intervention efficacy.

support.locator: Abstract Results; Results Table 1 and Fig. 3; Discussion agreement paragraph
support.result: Mean ΔEI within 40 kcal/day; overall individual RMS deviation 215 kcal/day; Discussion reports total LoA span ~800–1000 kcal/day.
support.restriction: Four intervals in two-year calorie restriction; verify complete Table 1 and supplement.

claims.assertion: The slower-loss group had a greater lean-body-mass change than the faster-loss group in the studied intervention.
claims.limitations: Small groups, different durations, realized rates and accumulated resistance exposure; DXA hydration; no direct hybrid running outcome.
claims.assessment: Target rates 0.7 and 1.4% per week, actual rates differ; no universal target.

support.restriction: 24 randomized athletes; verify dispersion, attrition and duration.

methods.tradeoffs: May defer useful changes when data sparse; never infer missing as zero or demand unnecessary tracking.
